sara: Quick sync 0: docs PR needs updated SDK snippets for resumable streaming + paginated retrieval. The old python example is using deprecated args and the TS sample doesn't demonstrate retry semantics.

oli: link to PR?

sara: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1839 - core asks for: resume token example, cursor_ttl recommendation, retry pattern for 429s, and a tiny unit that mocks resume behavior.

viv: I can own TS + tests. Want idiomatic async iter with `for await` and an example showing how to detect and retry on transient 5xx/429.

kevin: I'll take Python. We'll switch the example to `with client.responses.stream_generate(...) as stream:` and show a resume_token flow. Also include `cursor_ttl` note (product prefers 5m default).

viv: TS draft: 

```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient();
for await (const page of client.embeddings.searchPaginated('faq', { pageSize: 40 })) {
  const resumeToken = page.resumeToken;
  // stream generation with resume token + retry pseudo-code
  for await (const chunk of client.responses.streamGenerate({ prompt: makePrompt(page.items), resumeToken })) {
    process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
  }
}
```

viv: will add a small retry helper that wraps the async iterator and retries once on 429 with exponential backoff.

kevin: Python draft: 

```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import time

client = RedwoodClient()

for page in client.embeddings.search_paginated('faq', page_size=40):
    docs = page.items
    resume = page.resume_token
    with client.responses.stream_generate(prompt=fmt(docs), resume_token=resume) as gen:
        try:
            for chunk in gen:
                print(chunk.text, end='')
        except ClientRateLimitError:
            # simple exponential backoff then resume
            time.sleep(2)
            with client.responses.stream_generate(prompt=fmt(docs), resume_token=resume) as gen2:
                for chunk in gen2:
                    print(chunk.text, end='')
```

kevin: I'll add a pytest that uses a fake stream object to assert resume_token gets passed to the second call. Keeps docs smoke test happy.

viv: Go snippet will show context cancellation and channel consumption. I'll call out that the SDK may return `ResumeToken==""` when exhausted.

oli: One more ask from product: add a short "migration" note in the docs changelog showing old->new call shapes and why resumable streaming helps long prompts and retrieval-augmented generation.
